dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi hon, good morning. Fernando Amaral here. I got a drainage thing down the Point, and it's not even a storm thing, that's what's driving me nuts. It's dry out. It's been dry for days.
Okay, good morning, Mr. Amaral. Tell me what's going on and where you are.

11 Washington Street. The Point. So there's a snowbank, left over from the last plow, and it's sitting right on top of the catch basin. Right on it. And the melt comes down from the sun every afternoon and there's nowhere for it to go, so it pools all the way across the lane.
So the snowbank is covering the catch basin, and the water is collecting across the lane in front of your house. Is that right?
Right, right, across the lane. And then it freezes overnight, and then it thaws, and it just keeps going. I've been dealing with this on and off for, I don't know, two weeks now.
Two weeks. Okay. And is the water getting onto your property, or is it staying in the street?

Staying in the street, mostly. But the sidewalk, hon, the sidewalk is a sheet of mud and grit. All the sand and the dirt that washes down just gets left there. You can't walk it without ruining your shoes. My neighbor's got a little dog and she's carrying it.
Mud and grit all over the sidewalk. Got it. Let me write that down. Is it on the street side of Washington, or is it down toward a cross street?

It's right in front of eleven. Little bit toward the water side, if you're facing the harbor. Sorry, I'm in the car, I just came out to warm it up, and the heater in this thing has two settings, off and roaring. So I'm sitting here sweating with the window cracked, talking to you.

[pause] Well, at least you're not cold. I'm just going to read this back so I have it right. Eleven Washington Street, in the Point, a snowbank blocking the catch basin, water pooling across the lane, and the sidewalk covered in mud and grit. No storm, just melt. Correct?
Yes, that's it exactly. So who do I call to get it checked? Is that you guys, or is it somebody else? Because I called around last week to the, ah, I don't even remember who, and they said maybe.

It's us, Public Works. I'll put in a request for a crew to look at that basin and clear the snow off it. Whether it's the plow crew or the drainage people who go out depends on what they find, but it goes into the same request.
Okay, good. Because honestly it's the same thing every year. The plow comes through, pushes it all against the drain, and then everybody wonders why there's a lake.
I hear you. Do you want me to put a number on the request in case they need to reach you?
Sure, sure. It's 401-555-0165. That's the house line, but I'll hear it, I'm in and out.
Four oh one, five five five, oh one six five. Is that right?
That's the one.
Perfect. And is there anything else on the street, like a second drain nearby that's also blocked, or is it just the one in front of your house?
Just the one by me. There's another one at the corner but that one's clear, I walked past it. It's this one that's buried.

Okay, so just the one. I'll note that the one at the corner is working. Now, if it's frozen solid under the snow, they may have to chip at it a bit. I'd expect someone to get out there within a few days, probably early next week if not sooner.
Early next week. Hon, I'm gonna be honest, by then it's gonna be a skating rink out here. It's supposed to get cold again Sunday night.

That's fair. I'll mark it as ice potential on the sidewalk and the lane so they see it. That might move it up. In the meantime, if you can safely knock the top of the snowbank back off the grate yourself, even a little, it can help the water find its way down.
I can try that with the shovel. I didn't want to mess with it if it was a city thing.
No, that's fine. Just be careful if there's ice under it, and don't stand in the lane while you're doing it.
Okay, will do. Alright, well thanks for taking it down, Lorraine. I appreciate it. Hopefully somebody actually shows up this time.
I've got it logged, Mr. Amaral, eleven Washington Street, catch basin blocked by snow. If it gets worse or you see water coming toward the house, call us back right away.
Will do. Thanks, hon. Have a good weekend.
You too. Bye now.
